title: Introduce KV deflation path, spill circuit breaker and tenant pacing to reduce fragmentation-related OOMs
author: Marcus Chen
description: Motivation: production tenants intermittently hit OOM spikes driven by long-lived fragmentation in the KV cache when background spill/compaction lags under bursty write workloads. Existing heuristics evict by simple LRU+priority and trigger spill-on-alloc failures, but observed tail OOMs during high tenant churn and work-stealing. This PR implements a multi-pronged approach: 1) a lightweight 'deflation' path that coalesces fragmented segments in-place or via fast migration to reduce footprint without full compaction scans, 2) a spill circuit breaker that detects allocation pressure patterns and applies proportional backpressure and rate-limited spill amplification, and 3) tenant-level pacing to prevent a single misbehaving tenant from consuming disproportionate spill bandwidth and causing global fragmentation. Design summary: - Deflation allocator: new code path in src/kv/deflator.rs that scans per-shard free lists for high-fragmentation buckets and either (a) coalesces adjacent free runs into larger spans when contiguous, or (b) migrates cold records to the spill file using a fast-copy API which preserves KV metadata and invalidates old slots atomically. Deflation runs are rate-limited and piggybacked on the existing maintenance worker to avoid CPU spikes. - Spill circuit breaker: a state machine in src/kv/spill_breaker.rs which samples allocation failure rates, page reclaim latencies, and resident set growth. When thresholds are exceeded, it trips and: (i) signals the scheduler to temporarily increase eviction aggressiveness, (ii) throttles incoming write-heavy RPCs by returning a soft-429 with Retry-After when tenant pacing is enabled, and (iii) scales spill workers up to a capped burst. Circuit breaker resets gradually using an exponential backoff with hysteresis to avoid oscillation. - Tenant pacing: scheduler-level token-bucket per-tenant implemented in runtime/scheduler.rs; when breaker is tripped, tenants above their fair-share are slowed and long-running KV mutations are prioritized for deflation-friendly migration. - Metrics & observability: added kv.deflation.{runs,bytes_freed,failed}, kv.spill_breaker.{state,trip_count,trip_reason}, and tenant.pacing.{violations,avg_delay_ms}. Instrumented in Grafana dashboards and SLO alerts. Implementation notes: - New config flags (config/kvcache.yaml): kv.deflation.enabled, kv.deflation.max_bytes_per_sec, kv.spill.breaker.threshold_fail_rate, kv.spill.breaker.window_ms, kv.tenant.pacing.window_ms. Defaults are conservative (deflation off in older clusters by default; breaker enabled). - Added unit/integration tests under tests/kv_deflation/* exercising edge cases (concurrent allocs, partial migration failure, cancellation). - Added end-to-end canary harness in perf-canary/kv-deflation-canary that simulates 1k tenants with churn patterns. Benchmarks: - Synthetic canary: tail resident set (99.9th) down 22% on write-heavy workload, median allocation latency unchanged. - Production canary (internal): 40% reduction in OOM incidents across two impacted clusters during a 7d window; spill IOPS increased 1.3x but CPU overhead <5%. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag. 2) Enable deflation on canary clusters and keep breaker enabled cluster-wide. 3) Monitor kv.deflation.* and kv.spill_breaker.* for 72h; if regressions, revert deflation flag. 4) Progressive rollout to Dedicated and then Hosted. Backwards compatibility: deflation is safe across versions because migrations write to the canonical spill format; however cluster operators should ensure the spill store has >= 10% free capacity before enabling deflation aggressively. Migration/upgrade notes included in docs/upgrade-kv-deflation.md. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1437) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Canary harness - [x] Metrics + dashboards - [x] Config flags and defaults - [x] Release notes Draft - [x] Benchmarks attached (perf-canary report) Related work: builds on ENG-1024 (eviction priority refactor) and complements earlier compact-on-idle efforts (ENG-1310).
